title: A 30 percent assay adjustment removes most of the ALOHA particle N:P and C:P epoch falls
abstract: We test a documented particle-phosphorus assay change in the ALOHA record through 2024. Across 255 routine 150 m deployments, reported N:P and C:P fall by 25.6% and 26.9% between the 1995-2010 and 2012-2024 mean states. Dividing late phosphorus by 1.30, based on the reported paired yield difference, reduces these falls to 3.2% and 5.0%; conditional year-block intervals then include no change. Carbon to nitrogen changes little. This is an assay sensitivity, not a measured correction for all samples. A fitted phosphorus step near November 2011 remains positive after this adjustment and after season controls. Thus the method note does not explain the full local break. We also reproduce a published joint oxygen-nutrient particle-mixture bound. The adjustment retains a possible fit but raises its minimum selection factor from 14.17 to 17.39 and shifts the optimum toward old samples. The long-period phosphorus enrichment is therefore sensitive to measurement method, while the earlier mixture-feasibility result survives. These results do not apply to dissolved bottle phosphate, identify respiration or ventilation changes, or test basin-wide outcrop loss. Code, aggregate tests, hashes, source notices and independent computation checks are included.

display.caption: Annual particle chemistry and the sensitivity to dividing late particulate phosphorus by 1.30 at the documented assay change.
